source_artifacts.claim: Two for One defines a fixed, repeatedly emitted bubble, a low continuous floor, two high separated ducts, exits at those ducts, and no authored hazards or collectibles.

The collision loop records each player hit once; a falling Pac struck from above rebounds and continues without consuming the bubble, while a later ordinary hit applies the bubble effect and consumes it.
The movement engine lets a grounded partner carry a standing hero and accepts a buffered jump while supported by that partner; this supports Pac boarding and jumping away during Isp’s ascent.
At earlier level_24, the visible subtitle and authored route introduce Pac jumping onto Isp for a FLOAT ride.
At level_02, the author defines the first player-specific bubble effects and lists Pac top bounce and Isp FLOAT in the visible game card.

confirmed: The first pass correctly treated the idle WINDUP/AIMING/in-flight frames as environmental animation, not action feedback.
The first pass correctly recognized the earlier bubble effects and level_26 holder/catch cue as prior exposure; these are opportunities to learn, not proof of mastery.
The visible villain/dialogue cues do invite a bubble/projectile relationship, although no idle frame reveals the relation.
missed_mechanics: The first relevant use is not dodging or redirecting Gem’s projectile: Isp and Pac must ride/jump together to give Pac height, and Pac’s falling top-bounce is the first step of the mandatory route.
The top-bounce does not consume the same bubble. Pac gets carried to his duct and Isp later intercepts that same bubble for FLOAT and his separate duct/exit.
A deliberate Pac miss returns both heroes to the safe floor and repeats the boarding/launch; an Isp miss after Pac exits preserves Pac’s progress and only Isp needs another shot.
incorrect_inferences: No route claim in pass one was presented as fact; its alternatives were explicitly hypotheses. However the tentative “one victim” reading risks treating the visible villain line literally. Source shows one bubble can register Pac’s top bounce and later hit Isp, so that literal exclusive interpretation is false for this route.
changed_judgments: Reasoning changed from 2 to 3 because the mandatory plan has several interacting dependencies (partner boost, Pac’s top-side intercept, preservation of the same projectile, and Isp’s later catch) rather than a single untested projectile clue.

Cooperation changed from unknown to 3 because source and feasibility evidence require Isp’s lift and later intercept as well as Pac’s first intercept and exit; the roles are mutually dependent over several steps.

Execution changed from unknown to 3 because both characters perform controlled boarding/jumping/intercept/landing sequences. Several nearby simulations work, but they do not establish human or current-browser tolerance.
Timing changed from unknown to 2 because the one-second repeated shot schedule and multiple nearby feasible inputs show a real but repeatable intercept sequence, not a single narrow one-shot window.
Hazards changed from unknown to 0 because source defines no hazards and a continuous floor; documented misses return there safely.

Recovery changed from unknown to 2 because a Pac miss repeats the shared boarding/launch sequence, while an Isp miss repeats only the later catch. Both are recoverable without restart, but setup cost differs by actor and stage.

Novelty changed from 2 to 3 because earlier bubble effects and partner carrying are familiar, but the same projectile persisting through Pac’s special top bounce so Isp can consume it for FLOAT is a new causal model combined with those lessons. This is a source-aware estimate; human discovery evidence is absent.

Solution clarity changed from 2 to 3 because source exposes an essential rule not shown in the idle cue, and the dialogue literally says one victim/no sharing. The two-ideas subtitle is a hint but not an explanation.
unresolved: Whether new pairs discover the top-bounce-then-FLOAT sequence without the optional hint; source hint text does not prove base clarity.
Whether the existing branch and isolated source-fixture route have the same built-browser timing/visual presentation in current build.
Whether the 0.1-second span among a few simulated Pac departure times generalizes to a comfortable human timing margin; the traces are not exhaustive or measured-human.
Whether any alternative cooperative route also clears the current room; candidate-vs-unmodified comparison demonstrates a new feasible route, not impossibility under every other input plan.
Whether shared-keyboard users experience control friction or whether the bubble cap/contact cue is readable during play.

single_operator_note: One operator must control Pac’s jump off Isp at the ascent peak, then switch attention to Isp’s run/jump interception while Pac continues right and lands. The key clusters are separate but the narrow sequencing and two moving actors may add attention and hand-switching burden; this remains outside the two-human baseline and is not measured.
